title: AlphaEvolve Nudges Down the Matrix Multiplication Exponent
hook: The theoretical limit on how fast you can multiply matrices just moved: ω < 2.371177, beating 2.371339 — with ML-designed optimization and AlphaEvolve doing the refining.
key_points: The exponent ω bounds the asymptotic cost of matrix multiplication; the best bounds come from combination loss analysis, a refinement of the laser method.
Contribution one: reformulating the core optimization problem so it can be solved in a larger setting than before.
Contribution two: a new optimization algorithm for that problem, designed using recent ML advances.
Contribution three: refining that algorithm with AlphaEvolve, DeepMind's evolutionary code-search system.
Result: ω < 2.371177, improving on the previous best bound of 2.371339.
Author list mixes DeepMind researchers with complexity theorists including Virginia Vassilevska Williams and Josh Alman.
content_html: Improving the upper bound on the matrix multiplication exponent ω is one of those problems where progress is measured in the fifth decimal place and every step takes years. This short note from a joint DeepMind and complexity-theory team — including Virginia Vassilevska Williams and Josh Alman, whose own prior bounds it beats — moves it from 2.371339 to below 2.371177.
extra_html:
How it works

The current best bounds come from combination loss analysis, a refinement of the laser method developed over the last several years. At its heart is an optimization problem, and the paper attacks that directly in three steps: reformulate the problem so it can be solved in a larger setting than was previously tractable, design a new optimization algorithm for it drawing on recent advances in machine learning, and then refine that algorithm with AlphaEvolve.

Why it matters

The bound itself is a small numerical improvement on a famously stubborn constant. The interesting part is the method: this is machine learning applied not to guessing a mathematical object but to sharpening the optimizer inside an existing human proof technique — a division of labour that generalizes well beyond this one exponent.

related.hook: AlphaGo learned from human games. AlphaZero threw those away — one algorithm reached superhuman chess, shogi, and Go knowing only the rules and playing itself.
